scope: Ten authored source-informed cases, two scripted offer callers. No withheld samples, human clarity measurement, broad matrix or shared-module claim.
exploratoryPrior: artifacts/release-0.14/next-offer-counterexample.json already established the .9751 inspection counterexample. This is not a newly discovered or withheld result.
uncertaintyDefinition: A typed capacityUncertain=true requires the upper edge of the known 0.05 rounded-body bin to fail and the lower edge to pass. If both edges fail, the interval remains blocked. This is a pre-freeze source-review correction, not an outcome-tuned policy. Actual host admission stays authoritative.

callerContract: Decisions receive only detached actor/game views and own controller state. The conservative caller honors all unavailable flags; explicit-try may deliberately request an offer with capacityUncertain=true. Both prefer full repair when usable, then usable one-minute repair; otherwise take one paid available-recovery minute. After any refused Try, advance exactly one paid minute before reconsideration. No retry at the same minute, hidden-state admission probe or rendering request. For structurally impossible sends, both use visible supply/contact/budget information to stop immediately, even if the old copy reports capacity first. Camp retains its existing authoritative offers with no invented uncertainty; blocked Camp capacity waits one paid minute. Prefix requests are common prescribed legal host/player commands, not chosen from offers, and all prefix costs are reported separately. Receiver and physical host remain unchanged. Boundary cases stop at their goal, structural blocker or fixed cap; deadline continuation continues to minute 30 after release so endpoint service is recorded. No post-outcome tuning or new cases.
decisionRule: Report offer access, successful deliberately uncertain requests, refusals, blocked decisions, wait minutes, actual paid time/body/resources and endpoint work/service separately. No weighted score. A service tie is retained; fewer imposed waits may support only a narrow optional-control claim. No generic capability module is promoted.
